newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT says redundancies hit 1st qtr net.
newsitem.headline: PLDT says redundancies hit 1st qtr net.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co said on Monday its unaudited profits dipped 1.8 percent, to 1.28 billion pesos for the first quarter of the year because of redundancy costs.
PLDT, the country's dominant telecommunications company, said in a statement that the fall in profits was due to the 251.8 million peso cost of its staff redundancy programme.
"Without this unusual expense item, net income for the first quarter of 1997 would be 17.5 percent higher over that of the comparable period in 1996," PLDT said.
The telephone company said nearly 3,000 employees have left the company under the redundancy programme.
Operating revenues for the first quarter rose by 12.1 percent to 7.37 billion pesos.

The company said there was a slight reduction in its international long distance network revenues of 2.1 percent to 3.74 billion pesos. International calls account for 50.7 percent of the operating revenues.

The lower revenues from international calls was due to the combined effects of a reduction in international accounting rates, the promotional pricing programme of the company, and a slight depreciation of the peso versus the dollar.
Revenues from national long distance service, however, posted a sharp 40.5 percent climb to 1.26 billion pesos due to a steady growth in call volumes, PLDT said.
Local network revenues also rose by 28.9 percent to 2.30 billion pesos during the first quarter due to an increase in the company's telephone lines in service, the company said.
